title: Evidence Atlas
purpose: Compare measured, sparse, and unmeasured evidence across strategy features and regimes without treating missing evidence as zero effect.

bottomLine.finding: The atlas records where evidence exists, where it is sparse, and where no admitted comparison has been measured.
bottomLine.limitation: Sparse and unmeasured rows describe data coverage, not a zero or negative effect.
context: Paired deltas are not causal proof. Observational PF is route-level association, not causal lift or a promotion signal. Local volume is provider tick volume, not centralized exchange volume.

items.title: Regime matrix
items.description: The matrix is the principal Explore visual. Empty cells mean unmeasured, not zero effect.

items.title: Evidence detail
items.description: Every cataloged unit remains discoverable; status distinguishes measured, sparse, and unmeasured rows.

items.title: Method and limitations
items.description: The artifact builders keep this surface honest about what the numbers mean.
points: Paired rows are curated same-route baseline/variant comparisons; observational rows are route-level feature assignments, not pooled experiments.
Filters, entry triggers, stops, targets, and signal/context are separate roles; a feature can belong to more than one role in the source contract.

Paired lift preserves null metrics as unavailable, not zero. Observational PF describes historical route performance around recorded ingredients; it does not identify causal indicator or filter contribution.
Provider volume is tick volume, not centralized exchange volume, unless a source says otherwise. Regime labels are unknown when a source does not declare a trend/range target.
Absence from a measured row is not evidence of no effect. Research remains exploratory until it survives frozen-period, cross-asset, and forward checks.
